name: SAR Filing — Consent Hold (NCA Moratorium)
description: Sequence for the consent SAR path (EX-002). MLRO files a consent SAR seeking NCA permission before processing a specific transaction. NCA issues a 7-day moratorium. SVC-001 places the transaction on hold. NCA grants consent before moratorium expiry. Transaction released. If NCA refuses consent, transaction hold remains until MLRO manually resolves.
preconditions: Customer has attempted a specific transaction that the MLRO suspects is connected to money laundering
MLRO has decided to file a consent SAR — i.e. the MLRO needs NCA permission before the transaction can be processed
SARInvestigationRecord has been created (steps 1-5 of happy path are already complete)
Investigation and SAR preparation are complete (happy path steps 6-19)

steps.label: MLRO selects 'consent SAR' — seeking NCA permission for specific transaction
steps.detail: MLRO ticks consent_requested = true. Enters consent_transaction_ref (internal transaction ID).

steps.label: PATCH /sars/{id} — consent_requested: true, consent_transaction_ref: {txn_id}
steps.detail: SAR updated. consent_status set to awaiting_nca_response.

steps.label: POST SAR to NCA SAR Online (consent SAR flagged)
steps.detail: NCA SAR Online form includes consent request for transaction ref.

steps.label: NCA acknowledgement: 200 OK + nca_reference
steps.detail: SAR received. moratorium_expiry_date = filing_date + 7 calendar days. consent_status = awaiting_nca_response.

steps.label: Publish SARFiled (EVT-016)
steps.detail: Payload: { sar_id, customer_id, restriction_required: true, filed_at }

steps.label: Publish SARConsentRequested (EVT-017)
steps.detail: Payload: { sar_id, customer_id, consent_transaction_ref, moratorium_expiry_date, filed_at }

steps.label: SARConsentRequested consumed — transaction placed on hold
steps.detail: SVC-001 blocks processing of consent_transaction_ref. Fail-closed: transaction remains blocked until positive consent signal received.

steps.label: NCA issues moratorium notice (Day 1-7 window)
steps.detail: NCA notifies MLRO via SAR Online that a 7-day moratorium is active. MLRO receives notification out-of-band (NCA SAR Online portal).

steps.label: MLRO records moratorium notice received
steps.detail: MLRO enters moratorium details: moratorium_expiry_date, NCA reference.

steps.label: NCA grants consent (within moratorium window)
steps.detail: NCA issues consent grant via SAR Online. MLRO receives notification.

steps.label: Publish SARConsentGranted (EVT-018)
steps.detail: Payload: { sar_id, customer_id, consent_transaction_ref, consent_outcome: granted, granted_at }

steps.label: SARConsentGranted consumed — transaction hold released
steps.detail: SVC-001 releases the transaction hold for consent_transaction_ref. Transaction may now be processed.

steps.label: SARConsentGranted → WORM audit log
steps.detail: Consent grant recorded immutably with NCA reference and timestamp.

alternative_ending_nca_refuses.description: If NCA refuses consent (or issues a second moratorium extending to 31 days), the transaction hold remains. MLRO records the refusal via POST /sars/{id}/consent-response (consent_outcome: refused). No SARConsentGranted event is published. SVC-001 transaction block remains. MLRO must decide whether to close the account or seek further NCA guidance. This path is not fully sequenced here but the consent-response endpoint supports it.
alternative_ending_nca_refuses.account_action: Transaction block remains until MLRO manually resolves via separate account action

fail_closed_design.description: If SVC-014 experiences an outage while a consent moratorium is active, SVC-001 must NOT release the transaction hold. The transaction hold is fail-closed — it persists in the absence of a positive SARConsentGranted signal. This is enforced at SVC-001 level: the hold is only released on receipt of EVT-018, never on timeout or system failure.
fail_closed_design.regulatory_basis: POCA 2002 s338 — processing a transaction without NCA consent is a criminal offence
